authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: The company recorded impairment charges of $173.8 million, up from $3.9 million the year before.
Sonic acquired Harley-Davidson dealerships for its Powersports Segment, expected to add about $100 million of annualized revenue.
A cybersecurity incident at CDK Global suspended systems the company used. The company estimates it cut reported pre-tax income by about $47.2 million.
no_value_reason: debt is filed but interest expense is not

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and repeated in the 10-Q MD&A
business_model.claim: Sonic is a US automotive retailer that reports three segments: Franchised Dealerships, EchoPark (pre-owned specialty retail) and Powersports.
quotes: we had three reportable segments as of December 31, 2025: (1) the Franchised Dealerships Segment; (2) the EchoPark Segment; and (3) the Powersports Segment

business_model.claim: In 2025 the Franchised Dealerships Segment generated about 85.0% of total revenue, EchoPark about 13.7% and Powersports about 1.3%. Earnings therefore depend mostly on the franchised dealerships.
quotes: In 2025, Franchised Dealerships Segment revenue represented approximately 85.0% of total revenue (compared to 83.9% in 2024).

business_model.claim: Revenue comes from five lines. For the nine months to Sep. 30, 2026 these were new vehicles $5,204,200, used vehicles $3,980,500, wholesale vehicles $222,400, parts/service/collision repair $1,590,100 and finance, insurance and other (F&I) $614,100, against total revenues of $11,611,300 (all table in thousands). Vehicle sales are the largest lines.

business_model.basis: stated in 10-K MD&A and the 10-Q income statement
business_model.claim: Customers are mainly retail consumers ('guests') who buy vehicles and services. A small fleet new-vehicle business sells to companies. Nine-month fleet new-vehicle revenue was 65,800 against retail new-vehicle revenue of 5,138,400 (table in thousands).
quotes: New vehicle revenues include the sale of new vehicles, including new powersports vehicles, to retail customers, as well as the sale of fleet vehicles to businesses for use in their operations.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K, with the cost comparison read from the 10-Q income statement
business_model.claim: The Franchised Dealerships Segment sells new and used vehicles, runs service and parts departments, and arranges financing and aftermarket products. Service and parts work, including manufacturer warranty repairs, can be done only at franchised dealerships. Management says Fixed Operations carry a higher gross margin than vehicle sales.
quotes: Each of our franchised dealerships offers a fully integrated service and parts department.
Our Fixed Operations sales carry a higher gross margin than new and used vehicle sales and generally are not as sensitive to economic conditions as new or used vehicle sales.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1; the absence of a cost line is inferred from the layout of the 10-Q income statement
business_model.claim: F&I is a commission business. Sonic arranges third-party financing, extended warranties, service contracts and insurance and earns a commission. It accounted for $614,100 of nine-month revenue (table in thousands), and the income statement shows no cost of sales for it.
quotes: We also offer our guests the opportunity to purchase extended warranties, service contracts and other aftermarket products from third-party providers whereby we earn a commission for arranging the contract sale.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A
business_model.claim: The new-vehicle mix is concentrated in luxury and mid-line import brands, which management says typically have higher operating margins and more stable Fixed Operations. In 2025 luxury was 63%, mid-line import 23% and domestic 14% of franchised new-vehicle revenue.
quotes: For 2025, approximately 86% of our total new vehicle revenue was generated by luxury and mid-line import dealerships, which typically have higher operating margins, more stable Fixed Operations departments, lower associate turnover and lower inventory levels than other brand categories.

business_model.claim: Revenue is geographically concentrated. Texas was 26.2% and California 24.6% of 2025 total revenue.

Franchise agreements with manufacturers are a core dependency. Without them Sonic cannot buy new vehicles or advertise as an authorized factory service centre. This is also why warranty work stays with franchised dealers.
quotes: Without a franchise or dealer agreement, we cannot obtain new vehicles from a manufacturer or advertise as an authorized factory service center.

business_model.claim: New-vehicle profit depends on unit volume and gross profit per unit. In the 10-Q, same-store franchised retail new-vehicle gross profit fell 7% in the quarter and 13% over nine months. Management attributes this to price competition from higher available inventory and higher invoice costs.
quotes: Retail new vehicle gross profit decreased 7% and 13% during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, due primarily to increased price competition as a result of increasing levels of available inventory and higher inventory invoice costs, which combined to drive lower retail new vehicle gross profit per unit.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K risk factors; the revenue figure is from the 10-Q
business_model.claim: Used-vehicle profit depends on how inventory is sourced. Sonic gets much of its used inventory from trade-ins through its appraisal system, which it calls generally more profitable than buying at auction. Used vehicles brought in $3,980,500 of nine-month revenue (table in thousands).
quotes: We obtain a significant percentage of our used vehicle inventory through our proprietary trade-in appraisal system as this sourcing outlet is generally more profitable and more convenient for our guests and potential guests.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release
business_model.claim: EchoPark sells pre-owned vehicles and F&I only, with no customer-facing service. Its Q3 2026 growth is volume-led but profit is flat to lower. Retail used unit sales rose 22% to 19,923, while reported segment income was $2.0 million against $2.6 million a year earlier.
quotes: The EchoPark Segment sells used cars and light trucks and arranges third-party F&I product sales for our guests in pre-owned vehicle specialty retail locations and does not offer customer-facing Fixed Operations services.
Reported EchoPark Segment income of $2.0 million, as compared to $2.6 million in the prior year period, a 23% decrease year-over-year

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release; the 14-location comparison is from the 10-K
business_model.claim: Powersports (motorcycles, personal watercraft, all-terrain vehicles) is the smallest but growing segment. By Sep. 30, 2026 it had 46 franchises at 20 locations, up from 14 locations at year-end 2025 (per the 10-K), after April 2026 Harley-Davidson acquisitions the company estimates will add about $100 million of annualized revenue.
quotes: The Powersports Segment consists of 46 franchises at 20 locations (16 full-service dealerships and four authorized retail outlets) in five states.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q income statement and the earnings release; SG&A components are named only in the release's chart labels
business_model.claim: Selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expense is the largest operating cost after vehicle cost of sales. It was $1,338,400 against gross profit of $1,832,400 for nine months 2026 (table in thousands). Management targets SG&A as a percentage of gross profit, and Q3 2026 total reported SG&A was 75.6% of gross profit.
quotes: Focus on controllable selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses to maintain structural improvement in SG&A leverage as a percent of gross profit (compared to high 70% range prior to 2020)

business_model.claim: Fixed Operations revenue growth depends on service capacity and pricing. Same-store Fixed Operations revenue rose 1% in the quarter and 3% over nine months, attributed to added technician headcount and higher parts and labor costs passed on to consumers.
quotes: Same store Fixed Operations revenue increased 1% and 3% during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, driven primarily by increased service capacity as a result of additional technician headcount, and higher parts and labor costs that were passed along to consumers.

business_model.basis: stated in the balance sheet, income statement and 10-K risk factors
business_model.claim: Vehicle inventory is financed by floor plan borrowings, which adds a financing cost. At Sep. 30, 2026 inventories were $2,443,000, funded in part by floor plan notes of $2,076,800 non-trade and $211,200 trade (balance sheet in thousands). Nine-month floor plan interest expense was $64,700.
quotes: we are dependent to a significant extent on our ability to finance our new and certain of our used vehicle inventory under the Floor Plan Facilities

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q income statement and the 10-K MD&A
business_model.claim: Reported profit is also moved by non-operating items such as impairments. Nine-month 2025 results included asset impairment charges of $173,800, mostly on franchise assets. Nine-month 2026 net income was $159,400 against $71,800, so the year-on-year gain partly reflects this absent charge.
quotes: Impairment charges were approximately $173.8 million and $3.9 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the cited items (company self-description and store counts).
competitive_position.claim: Sonic describes itself as one of the largest U.S. automotive retailers by revenue. At December 31, 2025 it ran 111 Franchised Dealerships stores, 18 EchoPark stores and 14 Powersports stores. By September 30, 2026 the counts were 108, 18 and 20.
quotes: We are one of the largest automotive retailers in the United States

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the earnings release and the income statement.
competitive_position.claim: Third-quarter 2026 consolidated revenue and gross profit were all-time quarterly records, but growth was marginal. The 10-Q income statement shows revenue of $3,988,800 against $3,973,800 (table in thousands).
quotes: All-time record quarterly total revenues of $4.0 billion, up 0.4% year-over-year
all-time quarterly record total gross profit of $617.5 million, up 0.3% year-over-year

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the cited items; the SG&A mechanism is inferred from the F2 line items.
competitive_position.claim: Earnings fell despite record revenue. Q3 2026 reported net income was $41.1 million, down 12%, and diluted EPS was $1.28.
quotes: Reported net income in the third quarter was $41.1 million, down 12% year-over-year ($1.28 earnings per diluted share, down 4% year-over-year)

competitive_position.claim: Revenue is concentrated in the Franchised Dealerships segment, which was about 85.0% of 2025 revenue. EchoPark was about 13.7%, down from 15.0% in 2024, and Powersports was a small remainder.
quotes: In 2025, Franchised Dealerships Segment revenue represented approximately 85.0% of total revenue (compared to 83.9% in 2024).
In 2025, EchoPark Segment revenue represented approximately 13.7% of total revenue (compared to 15.0% in 2024).

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K; the margin benefit is management's belief.
competitive_position.claim: The franchised brand mix is tilted to luxury and mid-line import brands. Management says these typically carry higher operating margins, more stable Fixed Operations and lower inventory levels, which is a stated source of advantage.
quotes: For 2025, approximately 86% of our total new vehicle revenue was generated by luxury and mid-line import dealerships, which typically have higher operating margins, more stable Fixed Operations departments, lower associate turnover and lower inventory levels than other brand categories.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the cited items; the slowdown comparison is from the outlook bullet in P6.
competitive_position.claim: Fixed Operations (parts and service) is a steady, high-margin franchised strength. Same-store gross margin was 51.4% in Q3 2026 and revenue grew 1% in the quarter and 3% over nine months. Management says this business is less economically sensitive than vehicle sales.
quotes: Same store Fixed Operations revenue increased 1% and 3% during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively
Our Fixed Operations sales carry a higher gross margin than new and used vehicle sales and generally are not as sensitive to economic conditions as new or used vehicle sales.

competitive_position.claim: The core franchised new-vehicle business is under pressure. Q3 same-store retail new vehicle revenue fell 7% on a 7% drop in unit volume, and new-vehicle inventory days' supply rose to 65 days from 51 days.
quotes: Same store retail new vehicle revenue decreased 7% during the three months ended September 30, 2026, driven by a 7% decrease in retail new vehicle unit sales volume.
approximately 65 days as of September 30, 2026, compared to 51 days as of September 30, 2025
due primarily to increased price competition as a result of increasing levels of available inventory and higher inventory invoice costs

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factor and the earnings release outlook.
competitive_position.claim: Per-unit vehicle margin normalization is a named threat. The 10-K says gross profit per unit has trended down since the pandemic peak and may keep falling. Management nonetheless raised its FY2026 new vehicle gross profit per unit outlook range.
quotes: If gross profit per unit continues to decline, as we anticipate it may, it could adversely affect our business and results of operation.
Anticipate new vehicle GPU in the $3,050 to $3,100 per unit range for FY 2026 (previously $2,850 to $3,000)

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the earnings release and 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: EchoPark is growing quickly but earning little. Q3 revenue was $596.0 million, up 14%, and retail used units were up 22%, yet segment income fell to $2.0 million from $2.6 million, a 23% decrease.
quotes: EchoPark Segment revenues of $596.0 million, up 14% year-over-year
Reported EchoPark Segment income of $2.0 million, as compared to $2.6 million in the prior year period, a 23% decrease year-over-year

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q and earnings release; the 1.3% share is in P1.
competitive_position.claim: Powersports is a small but expanding third leg. It grew to 20 locations after an April 2026 acquisition, and Q3 segment income was $7.9 million, up 1%.
quotes: The Powersports Segment consists of 46 franchises at 20 locations (16 full-service dealerships and four authorized retail outlets) in five states.
Segment income of $7.9 million, up 1%, and adjusted EBITDA* of $10.5 million, up 4%

competitive_position.claim: A named structural threat is direct-to-consumer selling by manufacturers and new entrants. The 10-K says franchised dealers' role in that transaction type is unclear.
quotes: In addition, certain automobile manufacturers have expressed interest in or begun selling directly to customers.
Tesla, Inc. has been challenging state dealer franchise laws in many states with mixed results

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and business section.
competitive_position.claim: Sonic depends on manufacturers for its franchises, supply and acquisition approvals. Its franchise agreements are not exclusive and can be terminated or not renewed.
quotes: As a result, we are significantly dependent on our relationships with the manufacturers.

competitive_position.basis: Figures are stated in the statements; the funding mechanism is inferred from the cash flow statement.
competitive_position.claim: Financial flexibility is tighter in 2026. Nine-month operating cash flow was (14,500) against 500,500 a year earlier (tables in thousands). Inventories rose to 2,443,000 from 2,012,900 (table in thousands), and the 10-K says available capital is limited to debt-agreement liquidity and operating cash flows.
quotes: The amount of capital presently available to us is limited to the liquidity available under our existing debt agreements and cash flows generated through operating activities.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet (F1); the comparison of current assets with current liabilities is inferred from those lines.
financial_health.claim: Liquidity is thin on the balance sheet. Cash is only 10,700 (table in thousands), up from 6,300 at year-end. Current liabilities of 3,249,800 now exceed current assets of 3,089,800, whereas at year-end current assets of 2,832,500 exceeded current liabilities of 2,597,900.
quotes: Cash and cash equivalents | $ 10,700 | $ 6,300

financial_health.basis: Balances and days' supply are stated in F1 and P4; the link between inventory growth and floor plan growth is inferred from both rising together.
financial_health.claim: Floor plan financing grew with inventory. Non-trade floor plan notes are 2,076,800 (up from 1,748,100) and trade floor plan notes are 211,200 (up from 184,600). Inventories rose to 2,443,000 from 2,012,900, and new vehicle days' supply in the Franchised Dealerships Segment was 65 days against 51 a year earlier.
quotes: On a trailing quarter cost of sales basis, our reported Franchised Dealerships Segment new vehicle inventory days’ supply was approximately 65 days as of September 30, 2026, compared to 51 days as of September 30, 2025.

Floor Plan Financing arrangements allow us to borrow money to buy a particular new vehicle from the manufacturer or a used vehicle on trade-in or at auction and pay off the loan when we sell that particular vehicle.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet (F1); the shift toward current maturities is read directly from the lines.
financial_health.claim: Debt outside floor plan is large and a bigger share is now short-term. Long-term debt is 1,556,400 (against 1,563,000 at year-end), but current maturities of long-term debt rose to 193,300 from 52,400. Finance lease liabilities are 120,900 current (up from 19,200) and 286,200 non-current. Total stockholders' equity is 1,061,500.
quotes: Current maturities of long-term debt | 193,300 | 52,400

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated in F2 and F3; the comparison of interest with operating income is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Interest costs absorb a large part of operating profit. For the nine months, floor plan interest was 64,700 (against 62,200) and other net interest was 89,200 (against 82,500), versus operating income of 376,700 (against 244,300). Cash paid for interest was 136,600 (against 127,200).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement (F3); the explanation of the swing is inferred from the working-capital lines.
financial_health.claim: Operating cash flow was negative for the nine months at (14,500), against 500,500 a year earlier, even though net income rose to 159,400 from 71,800. The swing is mainly an inventory build: inventories used (415,400) of cash against a 62,100 inflow a year earlier.
quotes: Net cash provided by (used in) operating activities | (14,500) | 500,500

financial_health.basis: Line items are stated in F3; the funding interpretation is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Quality of cash generation is weak this period. Cash did not cover investment and shareholder returns. Purchases of land, property and equipment were 223,700 (against 112,600), purchases of businesses 169,300, treasury stock purchases 142,000 (against 44,100) and dividends 38,200. Proceeds from long-term debt of 190,000 were raised, and cash ended at 10,700 against 89,400 a year earlier.
quotes: Purchases of treasury stock | (142,000) | (44,100)

financial_health.basis: Amounts are stated in F1 and F3, and the capital-limit statement in P2 (from the 10-K, with the 10-Q noting no material change in risk factors); the view that new debt is the way maturities were met is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Near-term refinancing need is visible in current maturities of long-term debt of 193,300 and current finance lease liabilities of 120,900. The cash flow statement shows 190,000 of long-term debt issued in the period, and revolver borrowings and repayments of 40,400 each. The company says its capital is limited to existing debt agreements and operating cash flow, and that its dealership assets are pledged.
quotes: The amount of capital presently available to us is limited to the liquidity available under our existing debt agreements and cash flows generated through operating activities.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated by management in P6; revenue figures from F2.
growth_thesis.claim: In the third quarter, growth in EchoPark and Powersports offset declines in the Franchised Dealerships segment, leaving consolidated revenue only slightly above the prior year (3,988,800 against 3,973,800, table in thousands; up 0.4%). Continued consolidated growth requires the two growing segments to keep outpacing the franchised decline.
quotes: revenue and gross profit growth in our EchoPark and Powersports segments offset declines in our Franchised Dealerships segment

growth_thesis.claim: EchoPark unit volume is a growth driver: retail used unit sales were 19,923, up 22%, with segment revenue of $596.0 million, up 14%. This requires continued retail demand and an inventory build to support it.
quotes: EchoPark Segment retail used vehicle unit sales volume of 19,923, up 22% year-over-year
The higher days’ supply as of September 30, 2026, reflected a deliberate increase in inventory levels to support higher retail unit sales.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P6; the interpretation that volume is not yet converting to income is inferred from the stated segment income and F&I per-unit decline.
growth_thesis.claim: EchoPark profit conversion is the unproven condition: segment income was $2.0 million against $2.6 million a year earlier, a 23% decrease, despite higher volume. Growth in profit requires per-unit gross profit and SG&A leverage to stop eroding.
quotes: Reported EchoPark Segment income of $2.0 million, as compared to $2.6 million in the prior year period, a 23% decrease year-over-year

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P6 and P1; no figures for the cost or timing of expansion are given.
growth_thesis.claim: EchoPark's footprint is still being extended: a new Orlando market and a brand campaign are announced, and the long-term plan targets 90% U.S. population coverage at maturity. This requires capital and new markets to reach acceptable returns.
quotes: we are excited to announce our new EchoPark brand campaign and Orlando market opening in the coming weeks
we plan to continue to enhance our nationwide EchoPark distribution network to reach 90% of the U.S. population at maturity

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P8, P4, P1 and P6; the link from store count to segment growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Powersports is growing through acquisitions: five Harley-Davidson dealerships bought in April 2026 are expected to add about $100 million of annualized revenue, and the segment went from 14 stores at year-end 2025 to 20 at September 30, 2026. This requires smooth integration and continued deal availability.
quotes: is expected to add approximately $100 million in annualized revenue to Sonic's Powersports Segment
Powersports Segment Achieved Record Unit Sales Volume At The 86th Annual Sturgis Motorcycle Rally, Driving All-Time Record Quarterly Segment Revenues And Segment Income

growth_thesis.claim: Franchised fixed operations (parts and service) is a steadier but slowing driver: same store revenue rose 1% in the quarter and 3% for nine months, and management now guides FY 2026 same store fixed operations gross profit growth to 2% - 3%, down from mid single digit. Continuation requires technician headcount growth and cost pass-through to customers.
quotes: Same store Fixed Operations revenue increased 1% and 3% during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively
Expect same store fixed operations gross profit growth between 2% - 3% in FY 2026 (previously mid single digit percentage growth), implies 1% to 3% growth in Q4 2026

growth_thesis.claim: Franchised F&I is a stable contributor rather than a growth engine: same store F&I revenue was flat, with a 2% rise in gross profit per retail unit, to $2,630, offset by lower unit volume. It holds only if per-unit profit offsets declining retail units.
quotes: Same store F&I revenue remained flat during both the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively
Expect F&I GPU in the $2,600 to $2,700 per unit range for FY 2026, implies $2,550 to $2,650 per unit range in Q4 2026

growth_thesis.claim: Franchised used vehicles are growing in revenue but not in profit per unit: same store retail used revenue rose 7% in the quarter on a 3% unit increase, while gross profit per unit fell 3% to $1,506. This requires used-unit growth to continue without further per-unit erosion.
quotes: Same store retail used vehicle revenue increased 7% and 6% during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively

growth_thesis.claim: Franchised new-vehicle sales are the drag the other drivers must offset: same store retail new revenue fell 7% in the quarter on a 7% fall in units, and new-vehicle days' supply rose to 65 from 51. Any recovery requires affordability and inventory pressure to ease.
quotes: Same store retail new vehicle revenue decreased 7% during the three months ended September 30, 2026, driven by a 7% decrease in retail new vehicle unit sales volume.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures stated in F3 and F1; the link between inventory build and negative operating cash flow is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Acquisition and capex growth is being financed with debt, not operating cash: operating activities used cash of (14,500) in nine months against 500,500 a year earlier (table in thousands), while purchases of businesses were (169,300) and long-term debt proceeds were 190,000. Continued expansion requires access to financing and floor plan lines.
quotes: The amount of capital presently available to us is limited to the liquidity available under our existing debt agreements and cash flows generated through operating activities.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures stated in F2, F3 and P6; the attribution of the EPS gap to buybacks is inferred from the share-count change.

quotes: Reported net income in the third quarter was $41.1 million, down 12% year-over-year ($1.28 earnings per diluted share, down 4% year-over-year)

growth_thesis.basis: Inferred from the F2 and F3 line items and the third-quarter decline stated in P6.
